clue.text: Effective way for police to appear at a riot

definitions.meaning: a rule that is effective is operative, currently applying

definitions.text: way for police to appear at a riot
definitions.meaning: police arrive at a riot in large numbers, as a strong body

explanation.surface: A remark on what makes a police response to a riot work.
explanation.definitionFit: A law that is operative is said to be in force, and officers turning up en masse arrive in force: one idiom, two senses.

clue.text: Influence one Frenchman to get agreement

parts.note: one is I as a Roman numeral
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman
a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: Persuading a man from France to sign a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get' is a link joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Having an effect or a strong bearing on something is a common noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Corpulent single mother, Eastern maid?

parts.note: corpulent means fat
single means one, I as a Roman numeral
MA is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A stout lone parent described as a girl from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: a girl's name common in the Muslim world, after the Prophet's daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name widespread in the Muslim world, borne by the Prophet Muhammad's daughter, so an example of an Eastern young woman.

clue.text: Had children used the photocopier?

definitions.meaning: to have offspring is to breed
making copies of a document with a copier

explanation.surface: Did someone have kids, or just make some copies?
explanation.definitionFit: Bearing offspring and making facsimiles are both senses of copying again.

clue.text: He certainly didn't lose his marbles!

definitions.text: He certainly didn't lose his marbles!

parts.words: He certainly didn't lose his marbles!
parts.note: the idiom for going mad is reversed: this British earl kept the Parthenon sculptures he removed from Athens

explanation.surface: A man who was definitely still of sound mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose one's marbles' means go mad, but here the marbles are the Parthenon sculptures the seventh Earl took to Britain, now in the British Museum.
explanation.definitionFit: The Earl who brought the Parthenon frieze to London gave his title to those famous carvings.

clue.text: No longer a model for the investigative journalist?

parts.note: EX is the usual prefix for something former, no longer so
a model holds a pose, so is one who poses

explanation.surface: A former model has turned to investigative reporting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a model' looks like part of the career story, but it gives the word for one who strikes a pose.
explanation.definitionFit: A reporter digging out scandal lays bare wrongdoing, which is what one who reveals does.

clue.text: Let enamel designs be basic

indicators.note: designs suggests the letters are laid out in a new pattern

explanation.surface: Allow tooth coating patterns to be simple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'designs' rearranges the nine letters of LET ENAMEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fundamental or primitive, like the forces of nature, is rudimentary in this sense.

clue.text: Rose receives credit-card number by the weekend

parts.note: a PIN is the personal identification number used with a card

indicators.note: the end of 'week' is its last letter, read out of the word weekend

explanation.surface: Rose gets her card code sent by Saturday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' is a colour, not a name; 'weekend' is split as the end of 'week'. 'receives' and 'by' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale reddish colour is the shade also called rose.

clue.text: Perhaps it made Eve serve some pork

definitions.meaning: in Genesis, Eve was formed from one of Adam's bones, so jokingly an extra one he could do without
a cut of pork from the ribs with little meat left on

explanation.surface: A biblical tale where Eve offers a pork dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serve' is a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis says Eve came from one of Adam's bones, and the same phrase names a cut of meat from a pig's ribs.

clue.text: Ashamed, despite looking brave?

definitions.meaning: a brave is a Native American warrior, in dated and now offensive terms called red-skinned

explanation.surface: Embarrassed, though putting on a courageous face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brave' reads as courageous, but it is the old noun for a Native American warrior; 'despite' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassment brings a blush to the cheeks, and the dated stereotype pictured warriors with ruddy complexions.

clue.text: Proposed to go to and fro

indicators.note: something that can go to and fro, forwards or backwards, reads the same in each direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A suggestion that someone move back and forth.
explanation.walkthrough: The two words read identically left to right and right to left, which is what 'go to and fro' points at; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To nominate a candidate or offer a plan is to put it forward: a phrasal-verb synonym.

clue.text: Ideal country for the ecology party

definitions.text: Ideal country for the ecology party

parts.words: Ideal country for the ecology party
parts.note: a real Arctic nation whose name starts with the colour that names environmental parties, so it sounds tailor-made for them

explanation.surface: Which nation would environmental campaigners like best?
explanation.walkthrough: The ecology party is the Greens, so the joke is a country whose name begins with their colour; it is in fact mostly ice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arctic island nation's name begins with the colour of environmentalist politics, making it a punning dream state for that party.

clue.text: Commander got beaten up, but agreed not to prosecute

parts.note: COM is a dictionary abbreviation for Commander
to be beaten up is to be pounded

explanation.surface: An officer was assaulted but chose to drop the charges.
explanation.walkthrough: In law, to compound a felony is to agree, usually for payment, not to prosecute it.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal idiom 'compound a felony' means accepting a settlement in exchange for not bringing charges.

clue.text: Fellow recurrently dined on Greek cheese

indicators.note: recurrently suggests a word running back on itself, so the word for dined is read backwards

parts.note: dined means ate

explanation.surface: A man keeps eating a particular cheese from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurrently' reverses ATE into ETA; 'on' is a link placing it after F.
explanation.definitionFit: This crumbly brined curd, made from sheep's or goat's milk, is the best-known cheese of Greece.

clue.text: Labourite's about in regal style when put back

indicators.note: about means going round, so the Labourite's word surrounds the regal phrase

parts.note: a Labour supporter is a RED, a left-winger
in state means with royal ceremony

explanation.surface: A Labour politician behaves in royal fashion on being restored to office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labourite's about' is the Labourite is around: RED encloses IN STATE. 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Restored to a former post or position is the sense of returning someone to office.

clue.text: Risked being made to answer the phone

definitions.text: being made to answer the phone
definitions.meaning: someone summoned to take a call is brought onto the telephone connection

explanation.surface: Someone took a gamble by being forced to pick up a call.
explanation.definitionFit: To stake something is the idiom of placing it at hazard, while a caller is literally brought onto the telephone wire.

clue.text: Use the car too often in high gear

definitions.meaning: to drive more than is wise
a top gear reducing engine speed at cruising pace

explanation.surface: Driving excessively while in a high gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive motoring and a fuel-saving top ratio in a gearbox share this name.

clue.text: Fraudster made to pay for his crime in gaol!

parts.note: a con man, or con, is a fraudster

parts.words: made to pay for his crime
parts.note: punished with a money penalty

explanation.surface: A swindler punished for his offence, ending up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gaol' is British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut up or locked in, as a prisoner is, is the sense of imprisoned.

clue.text: Break journey to disrupt the cricket match

parts.note: to disrupt something is to stop it
an over is the set of six balls that makes up the unit of play in a cricket match

explanation.surface: Interrupting a game of cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an over is a set of six balls bowled from one end; the setter treats it loosely as the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Halting en route on a long trip for a short stay is the sense of the noun phrase.

clue.text: Failing to rectify the indolence

indicators.note: rectify means put right, so these letters are rearranged into proper order

explanation.surface: Unsuccessful attempts to cure laziness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rectify' reworks the twelve letters of 'the indolence'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weakening or deteriorating is said to be going downhill, a sinking idiom.

clue.text: Storage compartment used by a draughtsman

definitions.meaning: a sliding box in a chest or desk

explanation.surface: A drawer that belongs to an artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used by a' is a link joining the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliding box in furniture and one who sketches share the spelling.

clue.text: Squirm when serving court order on ambassador

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed on top of, so first in the answer

parts.note: a writ is a court order
HE is His Excellency, title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: Someone wriggles as a summons is served on a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when serving' is a link; HE, His Excellency, is how ambassadors are addressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist and wriggle in discomfort is a synonym of wriggling.

clue.text: Men of overfastidious habits

parts.note: men who fuss excessively over their clothing, 'habits' meaning attire as well as customs

explanation.surface: Men who are far too particular in their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: 'habits' reads as behaviour, but it also means clothes, as in a riding habit: these are dandies.
explanation.definitionFit: Dandies vain about their dress are the classic overfussy men of fashion.

clue.text: Commercial enterprise right for a speculator

parts.note: a commercial is an advertisement, an AD
an enterprise is a venture

explanation.surface: A business undertaking suits someone who likes taking financial gambles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commercial enterprise' looks like one phrase, but splits into an advertisement and an undertaking; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A risk-taker in business or finance, chasing gain through daring schemes, is an old sense of the word.

clue.text: Bear no right to invest

indicators.note: no signals the letter for right is taken away

parts.note: to bear is to endure

explanation.surface: Bear without justification to make an investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invest' here means endow with a quality, not put money in.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow or furnish someone with a quality is the old sense of the verb.

clue.text: Back in Southern Ireland you'll find its name

indicators.note: Back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Somewhere back in the south of Ireland the country's old name turns up.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft lacked an indicator for the hiding: 'in' marks it.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the poetic old name for the island of Ireland.

clue.text: Words of consolation always matter

parts.note: the setter wants the opposite of always, so the word for at no time
the setter wants the opposite of matter, its philosophical partner as in mind over matter

explanation.surface: A comforting phrase about things that will always be important.
explanation.walkthrough: Each word is replaced by its opposite: at no time for 'always', and the thinking self for 'matter', from 'mind over matter'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'don't worry about it' to a disappointed friend is the classic phrase of reassurance.

clue.text: That is how to transport a broken-down car

definitions.meaning: a formal phrase introducing an explanation, namely

definitions.text: how to transport a broken-down car
definitions.meaning: a broken-down car is pulled behind another, so the instruction is to haul it

explanation.surface: An explanation of how to move a car that has broken down.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal phrase 'namely' is used to introduce specifics, while split it says to haul the vehicle away.

clue.text: Grenade created disorder

indicators.note: the letters of the word are used to create a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An exploding bomb caused chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'created' reworks GRENADE; 'disorder' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To throw into confusion or upset the order of things is to disarrange, the verb's core sense.

clue.text: Doreen's been ordered to grant approval

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Doreen has been told to give her consent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doreen's' is Doreen has, so the S counts; 'been ordered' rearranges DOREENS.
explanation.definitionFit: To back or sanction something officially, as by signing a cheque on its back, is to approve it.
